question.text:
\[ P= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B= \begin{bmatrix} -7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \]

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2 \times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector $\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1,$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{c|cc} {\color{red}\lambda_1} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} \\ 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} \end{array}\right], \quad \quad P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_2)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

  • From our block diagonal matrix \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{c|cc} {\color{red}-7} & 0 & 0\\ \hline 0&{\color{blue}-2} & {\color{blue}5} \\ 0&{\color{blue}-5} & {\color{blue}-2} \\ \end{array}\right], \] we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\color{blue}\lambda_{2,3}=-2 \pm 5\textrm{i}}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\color{red}\lambda_1=-7}.$

  • From our matrix \[ P = \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}1&\color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}0 \\ \color{red}5 &\color{blue}0 & \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{red}0 &\color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are \[ \mathbf{v}_{2,3} = \begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{blue}\mp 2\textrm{i} \\ \color{blue} 1\mp \textrm{i} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}1 \\ \color{red}5 \\ \color{red}0 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text: \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \] Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2 \times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PBP^{-1}.$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector $\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1,$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{c|cc} {\color{red}\lambda_1} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} \\ 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} \end{array}\right], \quad \quad P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_2)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

\begin{align*} \det(A-\lambda I) &= 0 \\ \left|\begin{array}{ccc} -2-\lambda & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4-\lambda & 3\\ -5 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{array}\right| &=0 \\ (4-\lambda)\Big((-2-\lambda)^2 - 5(-5) \Big) &= 0\\ (4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 +4\lambda +29) &=0. \end{align*}

So, the real eigenvalue is $ \lambda_1={\color{red}4}. $ Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

\begin{align*} \lambda_{2,3} &= \dfrac{-4 \pm \sqrt{(4)^2-4\cdot 1\cdot 29}}{2} \\ &= \dfrac{-4 \pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\ &= \dfrac{-4 \pm 10\textrm{i}}{2} \\ &= -2 \pm 5\textrm{i}. \end{align*} Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

\[ B =\begin{bmatrix} \color{red}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}5 \\ 0 & \color{blue}-5 & \color{blue}-2 \end{bmatrix} . \]

question.text: Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2 \times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix: \[ \mathbf{v}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 5+7\textrm{i} \\ 1+\textrm{i} \\ \textrm{i} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \] The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=-1-2\textrm{i}$ and $\lambda_3=-2,$ respectively. Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_3}$ with corresponding eigenvector $\color{red}\mathbf{v}_3,$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_1} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_1} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}2},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} &0 \\ {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)}&0 \\\hline 0 & 0 &{\color{red}\lambda_3} \\ \end{array}\right], \quad \quad P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} \\ {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_1)}&{\color{red}\mathbf{v}_3} \\ {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}-2 & 0 \\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{red}-2 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector $\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_1,$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_3} \mathbin{:}$

\[ P= \begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}7 & \color{red}1\\ \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{red}0\\ \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}1 & \color{red}-2 \end{bmatrix} \]

question.text: Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2 \times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix: \[ \mathbf{v}_1=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1-\textrm{i} \\ -6+3\textrm{i} \\ -5\textrm{i} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad B = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \] The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=7$ and $\lambda_2=4+8\textrm{i},$ respectively. question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector $\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1,$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{c|cc} {\color{red}\lambda_1} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} \\ 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_2)} \end{array}\right], \quad \quad P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_2)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_2)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} \color{red}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue} 8\\ 0 & \color{blue}-8 & \color{blue}4 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} \mathbin{:}$

\[ P= \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}4 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1\\ \color{red}0 & \color{blue}-6 & \color{blue}3\\ \color{red}-3 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}-5 \end{bmatrix} \]

question.text: Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2 \times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices: \[ \mathbf{v}_1=\begin{bmatrix} -1 + 4\textrm{i} \\ -6 + \textrm{i} \\ 5 + \textrm{i} \\ 3-3\textrm{i} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 1 + 5\textrm{i} \\ -4-4\textrm{i} \\ 1 + 3\textrm{i} \\ -5-3\textrm{i} \end{bmatrix},\qquad B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \] The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=-2-2\textrm{i}$ and $\lambda_3= 4\textrm{i},$ respectively. Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\lambda_1}=\overline{\color{red}\lambda}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\lambda_3}=\overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}4}$

with corresponding eigenvectors

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} = \overline{\color{red}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}4},$

then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ {\color{red}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} \\ 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} \end{array}\right] \] and \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_3)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix \[ B = \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-2 & \color{red}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ \color{red}2 & \color{red}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}4 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}-4 & \color{blue}0 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3}.$ Therefore, \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-1 & \color{red}4 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}5 \\ \color{red}-6 & \color{red}1 & \color{blue}-4 & \color{blue}-4 \\ \color{red}5 & \color{red}1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}3 \\ \color{red}3 & \color{red}-3 & \color{blue}-5 & \color{blue}-3 \end{bmatrix}. \]

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} = \overline{\color{red}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}4},$

then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ {\color{red}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} \\ 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} \end{array}\right] \] and \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_3)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix \[ B = \begin{bmatrix} \color{red} 0& \color{red}4 & 0 & 0 \\ \color{red}-4 & \color{red}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}1 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}-1 & \color{blue}2 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3}.$ Therefore, \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-7 & \color{red}2 & \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}-5 \\ \color{red}-2 & \color{red}-7 & \color{blue}-7 & \color{blue}0 \\ \color{red}-2 & \color{red}-2 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{blue}3 \\ \color{red}-3 & \color{red}-2 & \color{blue}-5 & \color{blue}-5 \end{bmatrix}. \]

example.title: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix

question.text: Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2 \times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices: \[ \mathbf{v}_1=\begin{bmatrix} -3 + \textrm{i} \\ 5-2\textrm{i} \\ 2 + 4\textrm{i} \\ 3-4\textrm{i} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_3=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4-7\textrm{i} \\ 1-2\textrm{i} \\ 3 + \textrm{i} \end{bmatrix},\qquad B = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \] The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=-5+\textrm i$ and $\lambda_3=-3\textrm{i},$ respectively. Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
question.explanation:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\lambda_1}=\overline{\color{red}\lambda}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\lambda_3}=\overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}4}$

with corresponding eigenvectors

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} = \overline{\color{red}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}4},$

then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where \[ B= \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ {\color{red}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_1)} & 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} \\ 0 & 0 & {\color{blue}-\textrm{Im}(\lambda_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\lambda_3)} \end{array}\right] \] and \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ {\color{red}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{red}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_1)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Re}(\mathbf{v}_3)} & {\color{blue}\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{v}_3)} \\ {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{red}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} & {\color{blue}\vert} \\ \end{bmatrix}. \] Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix \[ B = \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-5 & \color{red}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \color{red}-1 & \color{red}-5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 0 & 0 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}0 \end{bmatrix}, \] we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3}.$ Therefore, \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-3 & \color{red}1 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}0 \\ \color{red}5 & \color{red}-2 & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}-7 \\ \color{red}2 & \color{red}4 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-2 \\ \color{red}3 & \color{red}-4 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}1 \end{bmatrix}. \]
